title: Global sections of an invertible module without common zero give a morphism to Proj of a polynomial ring over A pulling O(1) back to the module
statement: Let $A$ be a ring, $m\ge0$, and $P=\operatorname{Proj}(A[x_0,\dots,x_m])$ [def-pc-proj] ($\deg x_k=1$), with structure morphism $q:P\to\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] (on each standard open $D_+(x_k)=\operatorname{Spec}(A[x_0,\dots,x_m]_{(x_k)})$ it is induced by the ring map $A\to A[x_0,\dots,x_m]_{(x_k)}$), and let $\mathcal O_P(1)$ be the twisting module of [def-pc-projective-space-twist], with its basis $e_k=e^{(1)}_k$ over $D_+(x_k)$. Let $Y$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] with a morphism $g:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}(A)$; for every open $V\subseteq Y$ the ring $\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_Y)$ is an $A$-algebra through $g^\sharp:A=\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}A,\mathcal O)\to\Gamma(Y,\mathcal O_Y)$ followed by restriction. Let $\mathcal M$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_Y$-module [def-sc-invertible-module] and $s_0,\dots,s_m\in\Gamma(Y,\mathcal M)$ global sections such that $Y=Y_{s_0}\cup\dots\cup Y_{s_m}$, where for $s\in\Gamma(Y,\mathcal M)$ we put $Y_s=\{y\in Y:\ s_y\notin\mathfrak m_y\mathcal M_y\}$ ($\mathfrak m_y$ the maximal ideal of $\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ [def-weil-residue-field]). By [lem-weil-pbc-nonvanishing-section-trivializes] each $Y_{s_k}$ is open, and for all $k,l$ there is a unique $s_l/s_k\in\Gamma(Y_{s_k},\mathcal O_Y)$ with $s_l|_{Y_{s_k}}=(s_l/s_k)\cdot s_k|_{Y_{s_k}}$. Then there exist a morphism of schemes $j:Y\to P$ and an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_Y$-modules $\alpha:j^*\mathcal O_P(1)\to\mathcal M$ ($j^*$ the pullback of [def-pc-module-pullback]) such that: (i) $q\circ j=g$; (ii) $j^{-1}(D_+(x_k))=Y_{s_k}$ for every $k$; (iii) for every $k$, the ring map $A[x_0,\dots,x_m]_{(x_k)}=\Gamma(D_+(x_k),\mathcal O_P)\to\Gamma(Y_{s_k},\mathcal O_Y)$ induced by $j$ is a homomorphism of $A$-algebras sending $x_l/x_k$ to $s_l/s_k$ for every $l$; (iv) $\alpha$ sends the pullback $j^*e_k$ of $e_k$ to $s_k|_{Y_{s_k}}$ for every $k$.

source.place: Constructions, Lemma 01N8 (constructions-lemma-converse-construction) with d = 1, S = A[x_0,...,x_m] and the graded ring map psi: S -> Gamma_*(Y, M), a -> g^sharp(a) (a in A), x_k -> s_k, and its proof (psi_(f): a/f^n -> psi(a)/s^n on Y_s -> D_+(f) = Spec S_(f)); Lemma 01NA (constructions-lemma-apply) and Lemma 01NE (constructions-lemma-projective-space) for the case A = Z; the morphism lies over Spec(S_0) = Spec(A) because psi in degree 0 is g^sharp

proof.text: *The standard charts.* Write $S=A[x_0,\dots,x_m]$ and $U_k=D_+(x_k)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-proj-polynomial-twist-chart], the $U_k$ cover $P$, each is $\operatorname{Spec}S_{(x_k)}$, the ring $S_{(x_k)}$ is the polynomial $A$-algebra generated by the ratios $x_l/x_k$, and $\mathcal O_P(1)$ is free on $e_k$ over $U_k$. On $U_k\cap U_l$ the ratio $x_l/x_k$ is invertible, $U_k\cap U_l$ is its basic open, and $e_l=(x_l/x_k)e_k$. The structure map $q|_{U_k}$ is induced by $A\to S_{(x_k)}$.

*The local trivializations and ratios.* By [lem-weil-pbc-nonvanishing-section-trivializes], each $Y_{s_k}$ is open, $a\mapsto a\,s_k|$ is an isomorphism $\mathcal O_{Y_{s_k}}\to\mathcal M|_{Y_{s_k}}$, and there is a unique $a^{(k)}_l=s_l/s_k\in\Gamma(Y_{s_k},\mathcal O_Y)$ with $s_l=a^{(k)}_ls_k$ on $Y_{s_k}$. The assumed cover says that these opens cover $Y$. On $Y_{s_k}\cap Y_{s_l}$ uniqueness of the quotient gives $a^{(l)}_k a^{(k)}_l=1$ (since $s_k=a^{(l)}_ka^{(k)}_ls_k$) and $a^{(k)}_r=a^{(l)}_r(a^{(l)}_k)^{-1}$ (since $s_r=a^{(l)}_rs_l=a^{(l)}_ra^{(k)}_ls_k$). For $y\in Y_{s_k}$ the stalk $\mathcal M_y$ is free on the germ of $s_k$ by the isomorphism above, so the germ of $s_l=a^{(k)}_ls_k$ lies outside $\mathfrak m_y\mathcal M_y$ if and only if the germ of $a^{(k)}_l$ lies outside $\mathfrak m_y$, i.e. is a unit of $\mathcal O_{Y,y}$; thus $Y_{s_k}\cap Y_{s_l}$ is exactly the locus in $Y_{s_k}$ where $a^{(k)}_l$ is invertible.

source.place: proof of Lemma 01N8, first two paragraphs; Modules, Lemma 01CY

proof.text: *The local morphisms.* For each $k$, the universal property of the polynomial ring gives an $A$-algebra map $A[x_0,\dots,x_m]\to\Gamma(Y_{s_k},\mathcal O_Y)$ sending $a\in A$ to $g^\sharp(a)$ and $x_l$ to $a^{(k)}_l$; it sends $x_k$ to $1$, hence induces a unique $A$-algebra map $\rho_k:S_{(x_k)}\to\Gamma(Y_{s_k},\mathcal O_Y)$ with $\rho_k(x_l/x_k)=a^{(k)}_l$. By [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme], $\rho_k$ defines a unique morphism $j_k:Y_{s_k}\to U_k$. The same lemma and the basic-open description in step 1 give $j_k^{-1}(U_k\cap U_l)$ equal to the locus where $a^{(k)}_l$ is invertible, namely $Y_{s_k}\cap Y_{s_l}$ by step 2.

source.place: proof of Lemma 01N8, construction of $\psi_{(f)}$ and the induced morphism to $D_+(f)$

proof.text: *Compatibility on overlaps.* Let $V=Y_{s_k}\cap Y_{s_l}$. By step 3, both $j_k|_V$ and $j_l|_V$ land in $U_k\cap U_l$. Regard them as morphisms to the affine scheme $U_k=\operatorname{Spec}S_{(x_k)}$. Their ring maps agree on the polynomial $A$-algebra generators: $j_k$ sends $x_r/x_k$ to $a^{(k)}_r$, while $j_l$ sends it to $(x_r/x_l)(x_l/x_k)$, hence to $a^{(l)}_r a^{(l)}_k{}^{-1}=a^{(k)}_r$ by step 2. Thus $j_k|_V=j_l|_V$ by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme].

source.place: proof of Lemma 01N8, overlap identity for the maps $\psi_{(f)}$

proof.text: *Gluing the morphism.* By [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing], the compatible $j_k$ glue to a unique morphism $j:Y\to P$. Its inverse image of $U_k$ is exactly $Y_{s_k}$: the inclusion $Y_{s_k}\subseteq j^{-1}(U_k)$ follows from the definition of $j_k$; conversely, if $y\in Y_{s_l}$ and $j(y)\in U_k$, then $j_l(y)\in U_l\cap U_k$, so step 3 gives $y\in Y_{s_k}$. This proves (ii). On each $Y_{s_k}$, the map on the affine chart is $\rho_k$, so it is an $A$-algebra map and sends every $x_l/x_k$ to $s_l/s_k$. This proves (iii).

source.place: proof of Lemma 01N8, gluing the local morphisms and identifying inverse images of standard opens

proof.text: *The pullback isomorphism.* On $Y_{s_k}$, the pullback $j^*\mathcal O_P(1)$ is free with basis $j^*e_k$ by step 1, while $\mathcal M$ is free with basis $s_k$ by step 2. Let $\alpha_k$ be the unique isomorphism sending $j^*e_k$ to $s_k$. On an overlap $Y_{s_k}\cap Y_{s_l}$, the transition relation in step 1 and the chart map in step 3 give $\alpha_k(j^*e_l)=a^{(k)}_l s_k=s_l$; $\alpha_l$ sends the basis vector $j^*e_l$ to $s_l$ by definition, so $\alpha_k$ and $\alpha_l$ agree there. By [lem-weil-pbc-glue-sheaves-of-modules], compatible local module maps glue, so the $\alpha_k$ glue to an isomorphism $\alpha:j^*\mathcal O_P(1)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal M$; the local inverses glue as well. By construction it sends $j^*e_k$ to $s_k$ on every $Y_{s_k}$, which is (iv).

source.place: proof of Lemma 01N8, construction and gluing of the isomorphisms $\alpha_f$

proof.text: *The map over $\operatorname{Spec}(A)$.* On each $Y_{s_k}$, the composite $q\circ j_k$ is the morphism to $\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ corresponding to the ring map $A\to\Gamma(Y_{s_k},\mathcal O_Y)$ obtained from $g^\sharp$, because $q|_{U_k}$ is induced by $A\to S_{(x_k)}$ and $\rho_k$ is an $A$-algebra map. Thus $q\circ j_k=g|_{Y_{s_k}}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme]. The two global morphisms $q\circ j$ and $g$ agree on the open cover $Y=\bigcup_kY_{s_k}$, so they agree by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing]. This proves (i).
